'''Makeb''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] in the [[Aida sector/Legends|Aida sector]] close to the edges of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. It was a major source of [[isotope-5]], one of the rarest minerals in the galaxy.

==Description==
Located in the [[Makeb system/Legends|Makeb system]] in the [[Aida sector/Legends|Aida sector]]<ref name="EAOC" /> close to the edges of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]],<ref name="Rise">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel]]''</ref> in a region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] far from major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]], Makeb was an [[Ocean/Legends|oceanic]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Holonet" /> whose [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] featured enormous amounts of electromagnetic interference in its upper levels.<ref name="Atmosphere" /> The planet's gravity, while below standard, possessed unique anomalies that resulted in the formation of many massive stone pillars across Makeb's surface. The pillars, which reached high above Makeb's cloud layer and were often large enough to contain entire cities on the plateaus and mesas that topped them, were riddled with complex cave systems. The pillars and caves were home to both Makeb's native wildlife and numerous deposits of [[Mineral/Legends|minerals]],<ref name="Holonet" /> including the incredibly valuable [[isotope-5]], a mineral found only on Makeb, which was the reason behind Makeb's unique atmospheric and gravitational conditions, as the mineral had powerful warping effects on electromagnetic and gravitational fields.<ref name="Isotope-5" />

===Fauna===
Although Makeb was discovered relatively late, by the time of the [[Galactic War]] its indigenous fauna was already significantly mixed with alien species. For instance, yaracats, that became some of the most common Makebian predators, were brought to the planet by the settlers, when a breeding pair of the species escaped their crashed ship.<ref name="yara">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=codex|Yara}}</ref> Similarly, [[tonitran]], a jungle species native to [[Rishi/Legends|Rishi]], was also imported to Makeb where it was hunted by [[InterStellar Regulators|ExRegulators]] for sport.<ref name="regulator grounds">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=location|Regulator Bivouacs, [[Telemur Mesa]]|Makeb}}</ref>

===Infrastructure===
To connect various mesas and pillars of Makeb, a system of [[Light bridge]]s was implemented across the planet. During the [[Conquest of Makeb|Conquest]] of the planet, both the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] organized their own transportation systems connecting their camps, using [[Unidentified speeder van model|speeder vans]] as the taxi vehicle.<ref name="Makeb" />

==History==
===Early years===
As a result of its secluded location, Makeb was not discovered by the galaxy until the [[Mandalorian Wars]],<ref name="Holonet" /> a conflict between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior culture that lasted from [[3976 BBY]]<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> to [[3960 BBY]].<ref name="KOTOR 2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> During the conflict, a damaged transport carrying Republic [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]]&mdash;among them several wealthy businessman&mdash;crashed on the planet<ref name="History">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=codex|History of Makeb}}</ref> after being caught in the electromagnetic interference in Makeb's atmosphere.<ref name="Atmosphere" /> The businessman [[Semako Thalien]] assumed a leadership role among the refugees as they built settlements atop Makeb's pillars, and the colonists quickly discovered that Makeb possessed valuable [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]] deposits.<ref name="History" /> Forced to improvise mining tools, the settlers began to extract the minerals,<ref name="Mining">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=codex|Mining on Makeb}}</ref> and once they re-established communication with the rest of the galaxy, Makeb became immensely profitable for the settlers within fifty [[Standard year/Legends|years]]&mdash;a large part of which was the result of the influence and wealth of the original settlers.<ref name="Avesta" />

[[File:Talaos_City.png|thumb|left|250px|Talaos City]]
Remaining staunchly independent from the Republic, Makeb began to attract economic leaders, banking corporations, and wealthy tourists, leading to the rise in number of luxury resorts across the planet. The [[Avesta family]], a group of [[Human/Legends|Human]] merchant explorers, established a number of profitable settlements in the early years of Makeb's colonization, and they eventually established the [[Avesta Mining Corporation]]. The Avesta family also helped establish the [[Makeb Business Council]] - the planet's government, and members of the Avesta family negotiated a trade partnership with the Republic.<ref name="Avesta" /> The [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]] attempted to gain a foothold on the planet upon learning of its valuable resources, but the Business Council rebuffed their attempts<ref name="History" /> and forced the Cartel to negotiate a trade partnership instead.<ref name="Avesta" /> Over the following [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], Makeb grew in economic power, and though tourism accounted for a large amount of the planet's wealth,<ref name="History" /> mining remained the heart of Makeb's industry.<ref name="Mining" /> Makeb's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Talaos City]] was established near the original colonists' landing site, though the planet's inhabitants made an effort to keep industrial activities separate from the city. As a result, Talaos City became the center of Makeb's banking and technological economy and the heart of the planet's culture.<ref name="Talaos">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=codex|Talaos City}}</ref>

In [[3648 BBY]]<ref name="TOR_updates">{{TOR_updates|2.0}}</ref><ref name="regulators">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=codex|InterStellar Regulators}}</ref> a mercenary group [[InterStellar Regulators]] got an exclusive contract to serve as Makeb's security force. Until the later [[Conquest of Makeb|Hutt conquest]], they were respected and trusted by Makeb's people.<ref name="regulators" />

===Hutt Conquest===
{{Main|Conquest of Makeb}}
In [[3638 BBY]]<ref name="TOR_updates">{{TOR_updates|2.0}}</ref> the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutts]] outbid the [[InterStellar Regulators]] to serve the Cartel and took over Makeb, planning to use it's [[Isotope-5|Isotope-5]] deposits for a wider galactic conquest.<ref name="Countdown">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=faction|Imperial|Countdown to Doomsday|Makeb}}</ref> They initiated an intensified drilling, which destabilized the Makeb's core, causing severe ground-quakes and threatening to destroy the planet. The following crisis got attention of both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], which sent their teams to Makeb. While the Republic got busy evacuating the civilians,<ref name="TheArk">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=faction|Republic|The Ark|Makeb}}</ref> the Empire in secret devised a plan to save Makeb after everyone would leave, to secure the Isotope-5 for themselves. After the new Hutt [[Supreme Mogul]]'s death and Republic evacuation, Imperial scientists executed a rapid acceleration of the core-destabilization process, settling the core in a new state of equilibrium before it could explode.<ref name="Armageddon">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=faction|Imperial|A Cure for Armageddon|Makeb}}</ref> This however led to a cataclysmic series of ground-quakes, destroying most of the planet's surface. Newly stabilized Makeb got left exclusively in the Empire's hands, allowing them to freely mine Isotope-5.<ref name="Revenge">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=faction|Imperial|Revenge of the Archon|Makeb}}</ref>

During the crisis, [[Galactic Solutions Industries]] also became invested in Makeb. Their [[GSI Satellite Support system|satellite support system]] orbited the planet, providing assistance to GSI contractors traveling through Makeb on behalf of the company.<ref name="Makeb">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=location|Makeb}}</ref>

===Gethul===
In early [[3629 BBY]], an entity known as [[Gethul]], which had been buried beneath Makeb for millennia, was discovered by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Adelade]]. Though not yet fully awake, Adelade and her followers heard Gethul's "song" and fell under its sway, forming a [[Cult of Gethul]] and attempting to fully awaken the creature. Learning of this and fearing that in its full power Gethul could destabilize Makeb's core and obliterate the planet, Eternal Alliance military Admiral [[Bey'wan Aygo]] sent a strike team to stop Adelade's plan. The team was engaged by the cultists of Gethul, as well as Chief Engineer [[Penzaren]] and local wildlife, which Adelade and Gethul were also able to control. Eventually they reached Adelade herself and after defeating her in combat, detonated the [[D-5X]] probe droid loaded with explosives inside Gethul's maw, killing the abomination and stopping its threat.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Makeb_landscape.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Makeb landscape]]
The planet Makeb is the setting of the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel]]'', the first Digital Expansion for the [[BioWare]]-[[LucasArts]] video game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. Makeb was first mentioned in ''The Old Republic'' in a message from the [[Sith Warrior]] companion character [[Vette]]. The planet was released as part of ''Rise of the Hutt Cartel'' on [[April 9]], [[2013]] for players who pre-ordered the expansion, and went live for all players who purchased the game on [[April 14]].

Makeb has received the label of "the gay planet" as a result of BioWare's addition of same-sex romantic relationships to the non-player characters on the planet. BioWare had faced backlash because ''The Old Republic'' did not include same-gender relationships, unlike the company's past [[Wikipedia:Mass Effect|''Mass Effect'']] and [[Wikipedia:Dragon Age|''Dragon Age'']] game series, as well as their stand-alone game [[Wikipedia:Jade Empire|''Jade Empire'']] and even ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' in the form of [[Juhani]], the first lesbian to be introduced to ''Star Wars''. The developers promised that they would add the feature as soon as possible, but executive producer [[Jeff Hickman]] announced in [[January]] 2013 that the process's complexity meant that same-sex romances would not be widely available for some time. Hickman also indicated that the developers would compromise in the meantime, and the first major compromise is the planet Makeb. However, the decision has received criticism from newspapers and networks, as some writers compare Makeb to a segregated community only available to high-level players who have purchased the expansion.<ref name="Guardian">{{WebCite|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/gamesblog/2013/jan/25/star-wars-old-republic-gay-planet|text=Star Wars: The Old Republic, the gay planet and the problem of the straight male gaze|author=Mary Himlton|date=2013-01-25|format=Blog|archivedate=20200526215101}}</ref>
